relationships.evidence: Sulforaphane activates Nrf2-mediated cytoprotective and antioxidant pathways and has liver-focused evidence for reducing oxidative stress and liver injury.
Preclinical studies report antiviral activity of sulforaphane against multiple viruses; evidence remains predominantly cellular/animal rather than clinical.

Artichoke extracts containing caffeoylquinic acids have demonstrated choleretic activity, including increased bile secretion in a placebo-controlled human pilot study. Evidence does not establish that any single caffeoylquinic acid is solely responsible.

Dietary lignans are converted by gut bacteria into enterolignans such as enterolactone and enterodiol. A 2026 randomized controlled trial in perimenopausal women reported increased serum estradiol alongside increased fecal enterolactone, enterodiol and beta-glucuronidase after one month of lignan supplementation, supporting a microbiome-dependent phytoestrogen metabolism pathway. The evidence is still limited to a small clinical literature and does not establish a menopause treatment effect.

Soy isoflavones are dietary phytoestrogens and daidzein can be converted by intestinal bacteria to equol. Equol production varies substantially between individuals because it depends on the presence of equol-producing gut bacteria. The relationship is therefore directly relevant to phytoestrogen metabolism, but does not imply that soy isoflavones raise endogenous oestrogen.
